routineSummary: Given your stress but strong willingness to prepare, this plan focuses on a highly structured, day-by-day approach to maximize your 3 hours daily. We'll aggressively tackle your identified weak points (especially in Structural Design and key Architecture concepts), integrate FSRS reviews daily to cement learning, and ensure all subjects are covered. Remember, consistency and targeted effort are key to building confidence in these final 10 days.
anxietyAdvice: It's completely normal to feel stressed with exams approaching. To manage this, break down your study into manageable chunks, as outlined in this plan. Use the Pomodoro Technique (25 mins study, 5 mins break) to maintain focus and prevent burnout. Incorporate short mindfulness exercises or deep breathing during your 5-minute breaks. Remind yourself that stress can be a motivator, but it needs to be channeled productively. Trust the process, focus on one task at a time, and celebrate small victories to build confidence.

schedule.focus: Elementary Structural Design: CRITICAL - 'Doubly Reinforced Beam Analysis' (Tutorial 2) - detailed theory review and problem-solving practice. Theory of Architecture: CRITICAL - Address 'Architecture: Compositional Principles' ('i don't understand contrast') and 'Architecture: Spatial Enclosure' - review fundamental concepts, targeted FSRS practice. Engineering Hydrology: Initial study of 'Surface water hydrology' (Unit 1).

Elementary Structural Design: 'Flexure - Singly Reinforced Beam' (Tutorial 2) - extensive problem-solving. Theory of Architecture: FSRS Focus - Intensive review for 'Contrast of Form' (difficulty 1 despite reviews), 'Physical vs Perceptual Space', 'Scale and Proportion', 'Proportional Aspect Ratio', 'Contrast of Line', 'Contrast of Size' (difficulty 8 cards). Transportation Engineering: Initial study of 'Introduction' (Unit 1).

Elementary Structural Design: 'Bolted connection' (Tutorial 10) - theory and practice. Engineering Hydrology: Initial study of 'Hydrologic Abstractions' (Unit 2). Theory of Architecture: Initial study & FSRS for new concepts like 'Contrast of Tone', 'Accentuation and Rhythm', 'Mass Composition', 'Character in Architecture', 'Functional Character'.

Elementary Structural Design: 'Compression members' (Tutorial 13) - theory and practice. Transportation Engineering: Initial study of 'Highway Materials' (Unit 2) and 'Design and Construction of Pavement' (Unit 3). FSRS Review: Dedicated session for all pending Structural and Architecture cards, prioritizing recently studied topics or those marked difficult.

Elementary Structural Design: 'Slab Design' (Tutorial 7) - theory and practice. Comprehensive review of all RCC design concepts (Tutorial 1, 2, 3), focusing on interconnections. Theory of Architecture: Deep dive into 'Space and Architecture' (Unit 2) and related FSRS concepts ('Void and Mass', 'Enclosure and Boundaries', 'Color in Space Making', 'Material and Texture').

Transportation Engineering: Initial study of 'Traffic Engineering' (Unit 4) and 'Rail_ Water _ Air Transportation' (Unit 5). FSRS Review: Comprehensive session across ALL subjects, prioritizing cards with low stability, high difficulty (1-3, 9-10), or those approaching their review interval.

Elementary Structural Design: Rapid review of all units (Tutorial 1, 2, 3, 4, 5). Focus on key formulas, common problem types, and revisit areas where you felt less confident. Theory of Architecture: Review all units (Orientation, Space and Arch), paying special attention to FSRS concepts you previously struggled with. Engineering Hydrology: Review both units ('Surface water hydrology', 'Hydrologic Abstractions'), focusing on definitions and core principles.

Transportation Engineering: Rapid review of all units (Introduction, Highway Materials, Design and Construction of Pavement, Traffic Engineering, Rail/Water/Air Transportation). Consolidate key facts and figures. FSRS Review: Intensive session targeting *all* remaining 'difficult' (difficulty 1-3), low stability, or overdue FSRS cards from every subject. This is a critical consolidation day.

Mock Exam Simulation: Dedicate 2 hours to solving a full practice paper or a diverse set of problems from all subjects under timed conditions. Analyze Performance: Review your answers. Identify any remaining weak areas or common mistake patterns. Targeted FSRS/Review: Spend the last hour revisiting specific concepts identified as problematic during the mock exam.

Light Review: Quick skim of high-level notes, critical formulas, and your absolute 5-10 most difficult FSRS cards. DO NOT try to learn new material. Mental Preparation: Focus on relaxation, positive self-talk, and visualizing success. Ensure all exam essentials (ID, pens, calculator, etc.) are prepared. Prioritize a good night's sleep.
